# f5xc_fast_acl (Data Source)

FastAcl data source

The `f5xc_fast_acl` data source allows you to retrieve information about an existing configuration within your F5 XC tenant.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "f5xc_fast_acl" "example" {
  namespace = "example_namespace"
  name      = "example_fast_acl"
}
```

## Schema

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `name` (String) name This is the name of configuration object. It has to be unique within the namespace. It can only be specified during create API and cannot be changed during replace API. The value of name has to follow DNS-1035 format.
- `namespace` (String) namespace This defines the workspace within which each the configuration object is to be created. Must be a DNS_LABEL format. For a namespace object itself, namespace value will be ''
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `annotations` (Map of String) annotations Annotations is an unstructured key value map stored with a resource that may be set by external tools to store and retrieve arbitrary metadata. They are not queryable and should be preserved when modifying objects.
- `default_protocol_policer` (Attributes List) Default protocol policer Protocol rate limits to be applied if none of the source rules match. Traffic from source is classified into hash buckets based on first 24 bits of source IP address and rate limiting is applied on each hash bucket. This helps in grouping source IP address and ratelimiting traffic on that group, giving a semantics of hash limit for source IP (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--default_protocol_policer))
- `description` (String) description Human readable description for the object
- `destination_type` (Attributes) Destination IP type IP type specifies how to pick destination IP, possible options 1. Pick IP from physical interface 2. Pick VIP from interface or site 3. All VIP in site 4. Explicit IP and port (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--destination_type))
- `labels` (Map of String) labels Map of string keys and values that can be used to organize and categorize (scope and select) objects as chosen by the user. Values specified here will be used by selector expression
- `network_type` (Attributes) Virtual Network Type Specifies Virtual Network types on which Fast ACL must be applied RE applies Fast ACLs with network_type selector as 'public' only CE applies Fast ACLs with network type selector as 'site_local' and 'site_local_inside' only (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network_type))
- `protocol_policer` (Attributes) Default protocol policer Protocol rate limits to be applied if none of the source rules match. Traffic from source is classified into hash buckets based on first 24 bits of source IP address and rate limiting is applied on each hash bucket. This helps in grouping source IP address and ratelimiting traffic on that group, giving a semantics of hash limit for source IP (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--protocol_policer))
- `source_rules` (Attributes List) Source Rules List of Fast ACL rules to be applied to received packets on this site (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--source_rules))
- `uid` (String) uid uid is the unique in time and space value for this object. Object create will fail if provided by the client and the value exists in the system. Typically generated by the server on successful creation of an object and is not allowed to change once populated. Shadowed by SystemObjectMeta's uid field.

### Nested Schema for `destination_type`

Read-Only:

- `destination_type_choice` (Attributes) destination_type_choice The different choices for a destination (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--destination_type--destination_type_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--destination_type--destination_type_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `destination_type.destination_type_choice`

Read-Only:

- `all_services` (Boolean) All Services Destination will be a union of all VIPs covered via interface_services and vip_services option Port and protocol is picked up from listener config of each VIP Customer Edge: Applies the configuration to all the VIPs configured including interface_services VIP Regional Edge: Applies the configuration to all the VIPs assigned to tenant
- `destination_ip_address` (Attributes) Destination IP Address Destination is taken from configured ip address list Port and protocol are also picked from DestinationIPAddressType Customer Edge : Tenant can configure it Regional Edge : Tenant can not configure it (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--destination_type--destination_type_choice--destination_ip_address))
- `interface_services` (Boolean) Interface Services Destination matching any IP address assigned to the interfaces (e.g from DHCP) and participating as listener(VIP) Port and protocol is picked up from listener config of each VIP Customer Edge : Applies the configuration to IP of interface if configured for services Regional Edge : tenants CANNOT use this option on RE
- `selected_vip_address` (Attributes) All Service on List of Public VIP(s) Destination will be all VIP in List and services advertised on them. Port and protocol is picked up from advertise acl config of each VIP Valid only for RE. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--destination_type--destination_type_choice--selected_vip_address))
- `shared_vip_services` (Boolean) Shared VIP services Port and protocol is picked up from listener config of shared VIP Note: This option is available only for volterra administrators Customer Edge: Not applicable Regional Edge: Applies configuration on all shared VIPs used for services
- `vip_services` (Boolean) VIP Services Destination matching VIP configured as listener service Port and protocol is picked up from listener config of each VIP Customer Edge: Applies the configuration to VIP configured for services and does not satisfy interface_service option Regional Edge: Applies the configuration to VIP which has been assigned by default to tenant. Not applicable for shared VIP(s)
